links.outcome: Readability grade level of chatbot responses on knee osteoarthritis versus Grade 6 threshold
links.effect: All three chatbots produced text above Grade 6 (p<0.05); ChatGPT-5 most readable (FRES 45, FKGL 9.24, CLI 14.03, ARI 11.37).
links.quote: A readability analysis of responses from three different AI-based chat systems revealed that all platforms had text levels above the Grade 6 threshold, and this difference was statistically significant (p < 0.05).

links.outcome: Comprehensibility of AI chatbot patient information relative to recommended reading level
links.effect: Responses from all chatbots consistently exceeded the recommended comprehensibility threshold, making it difficult for patients to absorb information.
links.quote: When examining readability levels, responses from these tools consistently exceed the recommended comprehensibility threshold, making it difficult for patients to absorb critical information.

screen.reason: Evaluates readability, quality, and reliability of various commercial LLM chatbot responses (Perplexity, ChatGPT, Gemini) to patient queries about knee osteoarthritis without testing a specific deployment practice or guardrail.
